newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Russia in pact on cutting border forces.
newsitem.headline: China, Russia in pact on cutting border forces.

text.p: China, Russia and three other former Soviet republics have reached a comprehensive accord on reducing forces along their borders, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The agreement, hammered out after seven years of talks, was reached in the Chinese capital with representatives of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan as well as China and Russia, Xinhua said.
It gave no details about the timing or extent of troop reductions along the 4,300-km (2,580-mile) border.
The agency did not say when a formal pact would be signed but an accord has been widely expected in the spring of next year during a planned visit to Moscow by Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
Chinese Premier Li Peng is currently in Moscow for a trip aimed at paving the way for Jiang's visit.
China and the former Soviet Union clashed along their border in the 1960s when the two nuclear powers were rivals for the leadership of the world communist movement.
The old wounds were largely healed in the late 1980s and fears of renewed conflict have largely been relegated to the past.
Disputes over border demarcation were for the most part resolved in 1991.
However, technical problems of how many troops would be withdrawn from the border -- and concerns by Moscow of where they would be redeployed -- had drawn out the discussions, diplomats said.
The latest talks, the 22nd between the negotiating parties, were held over 16 days in a friendly and pragmatic atmosphere, Xinhua said.

Chinese Deputy Foreign Minister Zhang Deguang met the negotiators during their talks in Beijing. Ambassador G.V. Kireev led the delegation of member nations of the Commonwealth of Independent States, according to the agency.
The five states signed a landmark confidence building agreement in April during the visit to China of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
Under that accord they pledged not to attack each other and promised to inform the other states of the scope of military exercises along the border.
